inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average H1 2026 (10-Q 2026-06-30, XBRL WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding = 264.0m). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, buybacks are the funding mechanism (FY2025 $3,621m, H1 2026 only $280m while cash went to debt/investment).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K, AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $291m (XBRL). Equity-award tax withholding is not separately disclosed (buried in financing 'Other, net' $624m), so SBC is the expense line only; immaterial at ~0.1% of revenue either way.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), beta ~0.7 (managed care/PBM, defensive), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~7.8%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (interest expense $1.4bn on ~$31bn), 4.2% after tax; market D/(D+E) ~26% -> WACC ~6.9%, rounded UP to 7.5% and applied identically to all three scenarios. Regulatory risk (PBM delinking, FTC decree) is charged in the bear driver path and the 30% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases immaterial (~$130m/yr payments, <0.05% of revenue); left inside EBITDA/opex, no lease liability in net debt. One treatment only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: the EBITDA margin is anchored to pre-tax adjusted income from operations, which Cigna reports AFTER income attributable to noncontrolling interests ($475m FY2025; NCI net income $422m in H1 2026 alone). No further NCI deduction in the bridge (book NCI only $290m).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (engine route). Routing: Cigna is ~90% a health-services/fee business -- Evernorth (PBM, Accredo specialty pharmacy) is ~2/3 of adjusted operating income and Cigna Healthcare is predominantly self-funded/ASO employer business; after the March 2025 sale of Medicare Advantage to HCSC the risk-bearing insurance book is a minority. Its cash flow statement is a real operating-company cash flow (capex, working capital, taxes, interest on real bonds), so the SKILL.md 'insurer -> BVPS compounding' row does not fit: book value has FALLEN (equity 5y CAGR -3.6%) because Cigna returns ~all earnings via buybacks, and ~$73bn of goodwill+intangibles from Express Scripts dominates book. Insurance-specific handling: (1) net investment income ($1,046m FY2025) earned on float investments backing insurance liabilities is left INSIDE the operating margin and those investments are NOT added to the bridge (matching-asset rule, counted once); (2) only balance-sheet cash is netted against financial debt; (3) wc_capture set slightly negative for statutory capital that must grow with premiums. No prior DCF and no memory entry -- fresh build. MARGIN ANCHOR: FY2025 consolidated pre-tax adjusted income from operations $9,870m (after interest, after NCI, excl. $1,743m amortization of acquired intangibles and $1,046m special items) + ~$1,400m interest expense - ~$300m/yr normalised recurring special items = $10,970m attributable EBIT (3.99% of revenue); + depreciation of P&E/software ~$1,032m (D&A $2,775m less $1,743m intangible amortization) + SBC $291m = 4.47% pre-SBC EBITDA margin. Acquired-intangible amortization is excluded from D&A because it is book-only (Express Scripts was a stock deal; not tax deductible) -- putting it in D&A would manufacture a ~$370m/yr phantom tax shield. FY2026 guidance (Q2 10-Q / Analysis JSON): adjusted EPS >= $30.45 on ~264m shares = ~$8.0bn; / (1-21%) + interest ~$1.43bn - $0.3bn specials = ~$11.3bn EBIT on ~$290bn revenue (H1 2026 revenue +5.6% YoY) -> 4.37% EBITDA margin in Y1. CASH TAX: cash taxes paid ($399m FY2025) are depressed by $1,102m/yr of 'renewable energy tax credit equity investments' (investing outflow that buys tax credits); cash tax + those investments ($1.5bn) ~= book tax ($1.49bn), so the model uses the economic 21% rate, not the cash-paid rate. CAPEX: 'Property and equipment purchases, net' $1,212m / $1,406m / $1,573m FY2025/24/23 (10-K cash flow; untagged in XBRL, read from the filing) -> 0.46% of revenue. Investor Day 30 Sept 2026 will publish new multi-year targets; this build should be re-anchored after it.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Consolidated pre-tax adjusted income from operations FY2023-FY2025 ($9,318m -> $9,533m -> $9,870m), the company's own post-NCI operating profit series
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-2.1% 3y, -3.6% 5y) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (15.1% / 11.4%): book value shrinks because Cigna buys back ~all earnings, and revenue is inflated by pass-through drug cost (GLP-1/specialty) and the 2024 Centene PBM contract. Neither is a usable growth anchor; operating profit growth (~3%/yr) is.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; no interest income strip as Cigna is net debt): FY2023 $9,954m (OCF 11,813 - capex 1,573 - SBC 286), FY2025 $8,098m (9,601 - 1,212 - 291). Capex is not in the XBRL-built CSV for FY2020-FY2022, so 3y/5y FCF CAGRs are not computed. OCF is lumpy (receivable factoring, rebate timing, H1 2026 OCF only $710m), which is why the build is component-based and not anchored on any single year's FCF. GAAP EPS is distorted by the FY2024 VillageMD write-down and FY2023 tax items.

base.rationale: FY2026 on guidance; 2027 IFP exit; 2028 cost-plus/delinking conversion takes ~8% off the margin (4.37% -> 4.00%) and flattens revenue as rebates stop grossing up; thereafter operating profit grows with specialty/GLP-1 volumes at ~3-4.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Evernorth converts to rebate-free/cost-plus pricing (fully insured 2027, all clients 2028) and absorbs the 2028 federal delinking and the FTC consent decree at the cost of roughly one-tenth of its margin, but keeps its Big-Three scale and grows specialty (Accredo, GLP-1 management) volumes. Cigna Healthcare narrows to self-funded employer and international after the IFP exit; MCR normalises. Attributable operating profit dips in 2028 and then compounds ~3-4%/yr; capital return continues via buybacks and a growing dividend.
scenario_narratives.bull: Cost-plus pricing proves a share-winner: employers and health plans consolidate to the most transparent Big-Three PBM, the Shields/specialty investments and biosimilar/GLP-1 programs lift specialty mix, and the September 2026 Investor Day targets (high-single-digit revenue, low-double-digit EPS) are met. Margin holds through 2028 and edges up to 4.5% on specialty mix; regulation codifies a model Evernorth has already adopted instead of breaking it.
scenario_narratives.bear: Delinking and spread-pricing bans strip rebate and spread economics faster than service fees replace them; large clients (the HCSC services agreement, Centene-scale PBM contracts) re-bid on price against CVS TrueCost and Optum Rx cost-plus, and state PBM laws layer on further constraints. Evernorth margin falls roughly a quarter by 2029, revenue stalls in 2028 as gross-to-net presentation changes, and Cigna Healthcare MCR stays elevated on specialty/GLP-1 trend. Operating profit settles ~25% below the FY2026 level and grows only 2-2.5%; the market's ~9x earnings multiple becomes the right one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default because the profit engine depends on a single regulatory outcome (2028 delinking, FTC 10-year monitoring, state PBM laws) that is not yet priced by any disclosed contract economics. Base 50% as the company's own conversion plan plus guidance. Bull cut to 20% because it needs cost-plus to win share AND margins to hold through 2028 AND specialty mix to expand -- several independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Cigna as a fee-and-spread health-services operator, not as an insurer: the cash comes from Evernorth's PBM/specialty scale and ASO fees, and the book value is mostly Express Scripts goodwill that buybacks keep shrinking. The whole valuation turns on how much PBM margin survives the 2027-2028 rebate-free conversion and federal delinking; the base case assumes ~8% margin loss, the bear ~27%.
key_risks_to_valuation: PBM delinking (2028) and the FTC consent decree compress Evernorth margins more than modelled
Large-client re-bids (HCSC services agreement, health-plan PBM contracts) at cost-plus pricing
Medical cost trend / GLP-1 utilisation keeps Cigna Healthcare MCR above 84%
Revenue presentation changes under cost-plus (gross vs net) move the % margins even where dollars do not -- read the scenarios in dollars of operating profit
Investor Day (30 Sept 2026) may reset multi-year targets; re-anchor after it
Shields Health Solutions / specialty investments (~$3.5bn) and continued ~$1.1bn/yr renewable tax-credit investments are capital calls not modelled as growth capex
